scenario.title: Operating system and terminal differences
situations: A Windows user needs the supported Linux/WSL entry path.
A Linux desktop/browser needs system packages or sandbox setup.
A shell cannot find the installed launcher, or terminal/browser handoff fails.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Do not treat WSLg expected-to-work notes as verified compatibility.
Verify cross-platform examples against the installed release and preserve OS-specific recovery rather than making them mandatory branches.

lessons.title: Teach the active platform path only
lessons.when: At platform detection, a named prerequisite refusal, or a move to a different operating system.
lessons.need: Use the verified OS/harness combination and its filesystem, restart, permissions and login-lifetime rules; do not promise unverified desktop support from CLI support.
lessons.surface: WSL setup, launcher PATH helpers, terminal onboarding and Linux reference
lessons.gap: Coverage exists in several references but is not a complete tested scenario matrix. Review question: should FIRST-USER D/E expose per-platform evidence and offer only the active-platform recovery?

lessons.title: Resolve home and absolute globs on the executing machine
lessons.when: An unquoted filesystem glob is checked before a zsh command.
lessons.need: Matching ~/Downloads/Meeting* and absolute globs pass after home expansion; relative globs use the command working directory. Missing globs name the checked pattern and offer rg --files or a quoted tool pattern.
lessons.surface: Client-local and core unmatched-glob refusals share path resolution and repair helpers.
lessons.review: Source regression cases cover matching and missing home, absolute and relative globs in both hook paths, including a literal tilde directory and a home containing spaces. Live installed delivery remains unverified.
